title: The Security Of Practical Post-selection In Gaussian-modulated Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 September 2026;
tldr: This paper analyzes the security of practical post-selection in Gaussian-modulated continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD).
motivation: CV-QKD offers high key rates with standard telecom technology, but post-selection techniques used in practical implementations require rigorous security proofs under realistic conditions.
method: The authors develop a security proof for Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD with post-selection, likely using covariance matrix formalism, finite-size analysis, and composable security frameworks.
result: They derive secret key rate bounds and demonstrate that practical post-selection can maintain security against collective attacks under specified conditions.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical foundations and practical guidelines for secure CV-QKD implementations employing post-selection.

title: Decoherence-protected Entangling Gates In A Silicon Carbide Quantum Node
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 26 September 2026;
tldr: The paper reports decoherence-protected entangling gates implemented in a silicon carbide quantum node, advancing defect-spin platforms for quantum networking.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require robust local nodes that can generate and preserve entanglement; silicon carbide color centers are promising but are limited by decoherence during gate operations.
method: The authors implement entangling gates between spin qubits in a silicon carbide quantum node, using dynamical decoupling to protect against decoherence and achieve high-fidelity entanglement.

title: Ten-second Electron-spin Coherence In Isotopically Engineered Diamond
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 28 September 2026;
tldr: The paper reports ten-second electron-spin coherence in isotopically engineered diamond, a record coherence time for colour-centre spins.
motivation: Long electron-spin coherence is crucial for quantum memories, sensors, and nodes in quantum networks, but nuclear spin fluctuations limit it.
method: The authors use isotopically purified diamond (12C) to suppress nuclear spin bath decoherence and likely employ dynamical decoupling to extend coherence.
result: They achieve an electron-spin coherence time of ten seconds, significantly longer than previously reported in similar systems.
conclusion: This work establishes isotopically engineered diamond as a leading platform for long-lived spin qubits, with potential applications in quantum networking and sensing.

title: Fully Modulator-free Architecture For Quantum Key Distribution In Scalable Quantum Networks
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 24 September 2026;
tldr: The paper proposes a fully modulator-free architecture for quantum key distribution aimed at scalable quantum networks.
motivation: Conventional QKD systems rely on active modulators, which increase complexity, cost, and insertion loss, hindering large-scale network deployment.
method: The authors design and likely experimentally demonstrate a QKD scheme that eliminates modulators by using alternative encoding or direct modulation techniques compatible with network nodes.
result: The modulator-free approach enables simplified, scalable QKD nodes, potentially improving practical deployment in multi-user quantum networks.
conclusion: This architecture offers a promising path toward practical, low-complexity QKD for future scalable quantum networks.

title: The Equivalence Of Quantum Deletion And Insertion Errors On Permutation-invariant Codes
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 03 October 2026;
tldr: The paper proves an equivalence between quantum deletion and insertion errors on permutation-invariant codes, advancing quantum error correction for synchronization errors.
motivation: Quantum deletion and insertion errors pose challenges for reliable quantum information storage and communication, and understanding their relationship on permutation-invariant codes can simplify code design and analysis.
method: The authors establish a mathematical equivalence by mapping deletion errors to insertion errors (or vice versa) on permutation-invariant code spaces, likely using representation-theoretic or symmetry-based arguments.
result: They show that the error-correcting conditions for deletion and insertion errors coincide for permutation-invariant codes, implying that correcting one type of error suffices to correct the other.
conclusion: This equivalence may enable a unified treatment of synchronization errors in quantum codes, with implications for fault-tolerant quantum information processing.

title: Unitary Fault-tolerant Encoding Of Pauli States In Surface Codes
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 01 October 2026;
tldr: The paper proposes a unitary method for fault-tolerantly encoding Pauli states in surface codes.
motivation: Fault-tolerant encoding of logical Pauli states is essential for reliable quantum computation with surface codes, as these states underpin error correction and logical operations.
method: The authors develop a unitary encoding procedure for Pauli states within surface code architectures, likely using fault-tolerant circuit constructions on planar code patches.
result: The approach achieves fault-tolerant encoding of Pauli states in surface codes, presumably preserving code distance and logical information under realistic noise models.
conclusion: This work contributes a practical encoding scheme for surface code quantum error correction, advancing fault-tolerant quantum information processing.

title: Simulating And Sampling From Quantum Circuits With 2d Tensor Networks
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 24 September 2026;
tldr: The paper develops 2D tensor-network methods for classically simulating and sampling from quantum circuit outputs.
motivation: Classical simulation and sampling of quantum circuits is central to benchmarking quantum hardware and delineating quantum advantage, motivating efficient tensor-network contraction strategies for circuits on 2D geometries.
method: The authors employ 2D tensor networks (e.g., PEPS-like or projected entangled structures) with tailored contraction and sampling schemes to represent and sample from the output distributions of quantum circuits.
result: The approach enables practical simulation and sampling of quantum circuits whose structure is amenable to 2D tensor-network representations, providing accuracy/complexity trade-offs benchmarked on relevant circuit families.
conclusion: 2D tensor-network techniques offer a viable classical route to simulating and sampling from quantum circuits, sharpening the boundary between classically simulable and genuinely quantum-computational regimes.

title: Anomalous Weak Values In A Generalized Mach–Zehnder Interferometer Extracted Directly From Intensity Measurements
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 28 September 2026;
tldr: Anomalous weak values are extracted directly from intensity measurements in a generalized Mach–Zehnder interferometer.
motivation: Weak values typically require weak measurements and post-selection, making their direct observation challenging. This work aims to simplify the extraction of anomalous weak values using only intensity data.
method: A generalized Mach–Zehnder interferometer is employed, and intensity measurements are used to reconstruct the weak values without weak interaction or post-selection.
result: Anomalous weak values are successfully obtained directly from the measured intensities, confirming the effect in this interferometric setup.
conclusion: The approach provides a more accessible route to observing weak-value phenomena and may facilitate further studies of quantum measurement foundations.
